h: Sand, heath and a quiet swim
p: The name gives you a clue about the landscape here. This corner of North Lincolnshire sits on sandy ground, and old sand and gravel workings around Messingham have turned into lakes and wildlife-rich wetlands over the years. That makes the area a lovely spot for anyone who enjoys nature as much as fishing. Keep an eye out for herons stalking the margins, kingfishers flashing past and waterfowl on the open water.

Next door, Messingham Sand Quarry is a nature reserve looked after by the Lincolnshire Wildlife Trust, with lakes, reedbeds and birdlife that make it a nice walk for non-anglers in your group. A little further afield, Laughton Forest offers woodland walking, and Normanby Hall Country Park, north of Scunthorpe, has gardens, parkland and plenty for families on a dry day.

Practical bits: anyone aged 13 or over needs an Environment Agency rod licence to fish in England, and it's free for under-17s. Bring a landing net and unhooking mat, keep your swim tidy and take every bit of litter home, including line, which can be deadly for birds. If you're bringing kids, a short session with plenty of snacks beats a marathon one every time, and a float they can easily watch keeps them interested.
Weekends can be busier, so a midweek trip is worth considering if you'd like more choice of peg.
